title: Foundations: write, run and version code
goal: Become comfortable writing small programs in one language, using a terminal and Git, and reading a problem statement the way a contest or interview expects.

steps.title: The Python Tutorial
steps.note: Python is the fastest language to learn algorithms in, and it is the most used language with AI tools. Add C++ or Java later for contests.

steps.title: CS50x: Introduction to Computer Science
steps.note: Optional but excellent if you have never programmed. It also builds C intuition for memory and performance.

steps.title: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education
steps.note: Shell, editors, Git, debugging and the practical skills courses skip.

steps.title: Pro Git (chapters 1 to 3)
steps.note: Branches, merges and remotes. You will use these daily.

steps.title: Ship a command-line tool
steps.brief: Build a small useful CLI (a habit tracker, a markdown note searcher, a unit converter). Add tests, a README with usage examples and a license.
steps.deliverable: A public GitHub repository with at least 10 commits, tests that pass and a clear README.

exit: You can create a branch, commit, push and open a pull request without looking anything up.
You have solved 20 easy problems on a judge using the same language each time.
You can read a problem and state the input, output and constraints in your own words.
